subject: Compact SOC 2 Type II snapshot request + bridge letter options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@brightskyhealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compact SOC 2 Type II snapshot request + bridge letter options

Hi Alex —

Hope you’re well. We’re in procurement review for a production integration and need your SOC 2 Type II coverage details so our security team can sign off. To keep this light, could you share the following by EOD Tue May 25 if possible: 

- A copy of the SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) covering your most recent audit period
- The auditor name (CPA firm) and the report date
- A very small evidence snapshot: control owner matrix or a short CSV listing which systems/controls are in scope (example attached)

If your latest report’s coverage window doesn’t exactly match the calendar window we asked for, a signed bridge letter is fine — we’ve attached a sample bridge-letter for reference. We accept either:

- Full Type II report that covers Jan 1 2025 — Dec 31 2025, or
- A recent dated Type II + bridge letter that confirms coverage continuity for the procurement period we need

Transfer options: we can receive files via your SFTP (credentials to our secure intake) or you can upload to the secure link below. If you prefer, we can also accept a presigned S3 link.

Attachments (for your convenience):
- bridge-letter-sample.pdf (sample wording)
- evidence-minimal-matrix.xlsx (minimal artifact list we typically review)
- mutual-action-plan-template.docx (optional MAP for timelines)

Quick answers for our side: we need auditor name and the exact audit period on the report, a one-paragraph scope statement, and the minimal matrix. Redactions of customer PII are OK; please call out if anything is redacted.

Thanks — once we get these, security will confirm via a short intake call (15 minutes).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the clear note. We do have a Type II, but the report was issued Mar 3 2025 and covers the period 2024-03-01 through 2025-02-28. That doesn’t cleanly match your Jan–Dec 2025 window.

A couple questions:
1) Would that window plus a bridge letter be acceptable? We can provide the bridge letter signed by our VP of Ops.
2) On the evidence snapshot: is a control-owner CSV + one example artifact (access log export, policy snapshot) sufficient for your intake? We prefer to avoid sharing full logs unless necessary.

Also, how should we deliver the files — SFTP or the link you mentioned?

Regards,

BrightSky Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compact SOC 2 Type II snapshot request + bridge letter options

Alex — appreciate the quick reply and context. Yes, that’s workable. Short answers below and a couple of templates to make this low-friction: 

1) Bridge letter: acceptable. If your Type II end date is 2025-02-28, a bridge letter that confirms there were no scope or control changes between 2025-03-01 and our requested window (or that continuity is maintained through the procurement period) is fine. The attached bridge-letter-sample.pdf has two acceptable variants: (A) signed attestation referencing the existing report, or (B) a short CPA-backed addendum. Variant A is simplest.

2) Minimal evidence snapshot: yes — a control-owner CSV plus one representative artifact is sufficient for the initial intake. Preferred artifacts:
- a policy snapshot (PDF) for the control cited
- an access-control system export (redacted) limited to the control owners or a 7-day sample

Redaction guidance: redact only user-identifiable PII (names/email) if needed and include a short file-level note describing redactions.

3) Delivery: we can accept SFTP (preferred) — here’s a one-time intake path: https://redwood.app/sftp-share/BRIGHTSKY-REQ-98123. If you provide an SFTP username, we’ll generate the inbound folder and a presigned upload if required. Otherwise, a presigned S3 link works.

4) Timeline: if you can get the report + bridge letter + minimal matrix by EOD Mon May 24 (US/PST), that’s ideal. If you need more time, please flag and we’ll move the intake call.

I’m including two short one-line templates you can paste into procurement if helpful: 
- For procurement: "We have provided BrightSky Health's SOC 2 Type II report (issued 2025-03-03) and a signed bridge letter confirming coverage for the procurement window; artifacts shared via secure intake."
- For bridge letter signer: "The attached bridge letter is signed by our VP of Operations and references the auditor and report date."

If OK I’ll schedule a 15-minute intake call for Wed 20 May 11:00 AM PT to validate receipt and ask one quick clarifying question.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for looping legal and procurement-friendly language. Two quick notes from my side: 

1) Accepting a bridge letter is fine for initial procurement sign-off. Please capture exactly who signs (title + printed name) and whether the CPA is referenced. We typically accept a VP-level signature + statement that there were no material control changes; if a CPA attests, that’s even better.

2) For the evidence snapshot we prefer: control-owner matrix (CSV), one policy PDF, and one small redacted access-export (7-day sample). If BrightSky wants to avoid logs entirely, policy + matrix + statement of monitoring frequency is acceptable for now.

Procurement one-liner (approved):
"BrightSky Health provided their SOC 2 Type II report (issue date 2025-03-03) and an accompanying bridge letter confirming coverage continuity; intake artifacts were shared securely and reviewed by Redwood Security."

If you get the files, please drop them to the SFTP path and ping procurement@redwood.com to start the procurement record.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
